title: Cosy Systemtest
description:
End-to-end systemtest of the Cosy game-server platform: every night a GitHub-hosted runner installs Cosy from scratch with install_cosy.sh and drives 20 features through the real UI. One gauge sample per feature per run reaches SigNoz over OTLP.

READ FIRST — this dashboard is EXPECTED to show 2 reds and 1 skip. EXPECTED REDS: `templates` and `server-from-template` fail on a confirmed bug in the RELEASED product (v1.0.3 strict-compares a string template game_id against a numeric games-API id, so the wizard never lists a template). EXPECTED SKIP: `rcon` is quarantined behind SYSTEMTEST_HEAVY because Minecraft does not boot within budget on a GitHub-hosted runner. Details: https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

Channels: `release` = the installer exactly as published (nightly 02:30 UTC + release tags); `staging` = the same suite against freshly pushed sha-<short> images.

Every query wraps its metric in last_over_time(...[26h]) because a nightly publishes one sample per day and Prometheus' 5-minute lookback would otherwise blank the whole dashboard minutes after a run. Source of truth for this JSON: https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/signoz-dashboard.json

NOTE (2026-07-25): the metrics were renamed to the cosy_platform_ prefix on that day. The release-channel panels stay empty until the first nightly publishes under the new names; earlier runs are still in SigNoz under cosy_systemtest_*, which now belongs exclusively to the unrelated Cosy Domain Provider systemtest — do not query it here.

TRACES (since 2026-07-25): every run also emits ONE trace — a root span `cosy-systemtest run (<channel>)` with one child span per feature, carrying the same resource attributes as the metrics. Use it to see the run as a timeline instead of a matrix. Get there from the "Runs in window" table (row → "Open this run's trace"), or search the Traces explorer for service.name=cosy-systemtest. A skipped feature appears as a ZERO-LENGTH span named `<feature> [skipped]` with span status UNSET — never OK, so a skip can never read as a pass.

widgets.title: Unexpected failures (release)
widgets.description: Failing features EXCLUDING the two that fail on the documented released-product bug (templates, server-from-template). This is the tile that means 'something new broke'; red here is a real regression. When the fix ships, drop the exclusion from this panel and from the CosySystemtestFeatureFailing alert rule — the CosySystemtestKnownBugFixed rule mails a reminder. https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

widgets.title: Skipped (release)
widgets.description: Features that did NOT run. Expected: 1 (`rcon`, quarantined behind SYSTEMTEST_HEAVY). More than one means a feature silently stopped being tested. https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

widgets.title: Features reported (release)
widgets.description: Total feature rows in the last run — every feature reports feature_skipped, so this is the matrix size. Expected: 20. A drop means the run was cut short (or a spec file vanished) and the other tiles are counting an incomplete matrix.

widgets.title: Hours since last release run
widgets.description: Freshness. The nightly runs at 02:30 UTC, so this should stay under 26 h. 999 means no release run has reported for at least 7 days. Alert: CosySystemtestStale.

widgets.title: Feature × time — release
widgets.description: When a feature broke and for how long. Values are carried forward for 26 h, so one nightly sample draws a full day-wide step rather than a dot.

widgets.title: Failing features over time (release)
widgets.description: Stacked band per FAILING feature — the stack height is how many features are red and each band shows exactly when that feature broke and when it recovered. Passing features are filtered out, so the legend only ever names what is actually broken. The two permanent bands are the documented product bug. https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

widgets.title: Feature status over time — every feature (release)
widgets.description: 1 = passed, 0 = failed, gap = the feature did not run (skips are deliberately absent from this metric — see 'Features not running' below). Use the legend to isolate a single feature's history.

widgets.title: Features not running over time (release)
widgets.description: A line here means the feature was SKIPPED — untested, which is neither a pass nor a fail. `rcon` is expected. Any other feature appearing here is a coverage regression and is alerted on by CosySystemtestFeatureNotRunning.

widgets.title: Duration trends (release)
widgets.description: Creeping slowness shows up here long before it turns into a timeout.

widgets.title: Feature duration (release)
widgets.description: Wall-clock seconds per feature per run. Skipped features are absent rather than 0, so a quarantined feature cannot masquerade as 'it got fast'.

widgets.title: Suite time (release)
widgets.description: Sum of all feature durations in the last run. The CI job has timeout-minutes: 60; a run that approaches it starts losing features to cancellation.

widgets.title: Slowest feature (release)
widgets.description: Duration of the single slowest feature in the last run.

widgets.title: Features over 120 s (release)
widgets.description: How many features individually took more than two minutes. Watch the trend, not the absolute number — the heavyweight template/Minecraft paths are legitimately slow.

widgets.title: Build under test & drill-down
widgets.description: Which images produced these results, and the GitHub run that recorded them.

widgets.title: Runs in window — image tags, GitHub run link & trace
widgets.description:
One row per run in the dashboard's time range, carrying the resource attributes every data point is tagged with. A red cell in the matrix above is attributable to the backend/frontend image tag here; the run URL leads to the Playwright HTML report, traces and videos, and cosy.systemtest.trace_id identifies the OTLP trace the same run emitted — the per-feature timeline (what ran when, how long, which failed and why).

DRILL-DOWN: click a row and choose "Open this run's trace" to jump to /trace/<id> in SigNoz. The id is also shown as a column, so it can be pasted into the Traces explorer's trace-id search if the context menu is unavailable.

(Builder query rather than PromQL: the attribute keys contain dots, which PromQL label names cannot express.)

widgets.title: Staging channel — pre-release builds (heads-up, not an incident)
widgets.description: The staging channel installs a freshly pushed sha-<short> image instead of the published tags, so it answers 'will the NEXT release break this?'. Runs are push-triggered, not nightly, so these tiles look back 7 days and going quiet is normal. Alerting on this channel is notification-only (severity: info).

widgets.title: Passing (staging)
widgets.description: Features that passed in the most recent staging run (7-day lookback).

widgets.title: Failing (staging)
widgets.description: Features that failed in the most recent staging run. NOT excluded from the known product-bug list on purpose: the template fix is already on frontend main, so these two going green here is the signal that the next release repairs them.

widgets.title: Skipped (staging)
widgets.description: Features that did not run in the most recent staging run.

widgets.title: Hours since last staging run
widgets.description: Staging is push-triggered, so a large value means nobody pushed — not a fault. 999 = no staging run in 30 days (expected until the Phase 4 dispatch hooks land).

widgets.title: Failing features over time (staging)
widgets.description: Same stacked-band view as the release matrix, for the pre-release build. A band that exists here but not on release = the next version regresses that feature. A band that exists on release but not here = the next version fixes it.

widgets.title: Known expected reds & skips — read this before triaging
widgets.description: EXPECTED REDS: `templates` and `server-from-template` fail on a confirmed bug in the RELEASED product (v1.0.3 strict-compares a string template game_id against a numeric games-API id, so the wizard never lists a template). EXPECTED SKIP: `rcon` is quarantined behind SYSTEMTEST_HEAVY because Minecraft does not boot within budget on a GitHub-hosted runner. Details: https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

widgets.title: Known product-bug reds (expected 2)
widgets.description: `templates` and `server-from-template` are RED on purpose: released v1.0.3 compares a string template `game_id` against the numeric `external_game_id` from the games API, so the create wizard always reports 'No templates are available for this game'. Fixed on frontend main, unreleased. The specs are deliberately NOT skipped — they are detecting a genuine broken feature, and will go green on their own when a release ships the fix. Expected value: 2. If this reads 0, the fix has shipped: remove the feature!~"templates|server-from-template" exclusion from the 'Unexpected failures' tile and from the CosySystemtestFeatureFailing alert. https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md

widgets.title: Intentional skips (expected 1: rcon)
widgets.description: `rcon` is quarantined behind SYSTEMTEST_HEAVY: across runs 12-15 Minecraft (itzg, TYPE=PAPER) never reached a stable RUNNING within the 7-minute ready budget on a 4-vCPU GitHub-hosted runner, at ~20 minutes per attempt. RCON is therefore UNVERIFIED in CI — it is exercised only with SYSTEMTEST_HEAVY=1 locally or on a larger runner. Expected value: 1. https://github.com/Magenta-Mause/Cosy-Systemtest/blob/main/docs/KNOWN-ISSUES.md
